_nota: Version 3. Identica a v2 salvo CONTACTO_EXPERIENCIAL, reescrito para separar el eje INSTRUMENTAL (como se produce el conocimiento) del eje TEMATICO (de que trata). El descriptor anterior correlacionaba 0.936 con SOCIAL_HUMANA porque compartia el vocabulario de la experiencia vivida y de las personas. Esta version elimina toda palabra de tema -movilidad, ciudad, experiencia, personas, desigualdad- y deja unicamente procedimientos y materiales de investigacion, al mismo nivel de abstraccion en que TECNICISTA lista sus instrumentos. Se convierte asi en el polo opuesto de TECNICISTA dentro del mismo eje. El filtro de relevancia garantiza que el dominio sigue acotado.

relevance.URBAN_MOBILITY_TRANSPORT: Research in which the substantive object of study is the physical movement, travel, accessibility, or transportation of people or goods within an urban or metropolitan context. This includes urban public transport, buses, metro, tram and rail services; private vehicle travel and urban traffic; walking, cycling and active mobility; commuting, trips and travel; passenger movement; urban freight and city logistics; transport networks, services, infrastructure, planning and operations when these are examined as components of urban mobility or transportation. The defining criterion is that urban mobility or urban transport itself constitutes a central object of the research rather than merely an incidental application context.

dimensions.TECNICISTA: Urban mobility or transport approached as a system, network, infrastructure, or operation whose functioning, efficiency, performance, cost, design, prediction, control, or optimization constitutes the central research problem. This includes route and network optimization, traffic flow, congestion, scheduling and frequencies, capacity, level of service, reliability, and intelligent transportation systems; the economic evaluation of transport through operating costs, cost-benefit analysis, pricing, fares, tolls, demand modelling, generalized cost, and economic efficiency; and the instruments through which this knowledge is produced, namely mathematical and statistical modelling, econometric estimation, regression and discrete choice models, traffic and transport simulation, forecasting, algorithms, optimization procedures, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and the exploitation of large-scale digital datasets, sensor records, and big data sources.
dimensions.AMBIENTAL: Environmental impacts, externalities, or consequences of urban mobility or transport, substantively measured, modelled, or evaluated. This includes greenhouse gas and CO2 emissions, air pollution and air quality, traffic noise, energy consumption, fossil fuel use, climate change, carbon footprint, decarbonization, life-cycle assessment, environmental sustainability and sustainable mobility, and ecological impacts directly attributable to transport systems and mobility practices.
dimensions.SOCIAL_HUMANA: Urban mobility or transport examined in relation to people, social groups, and human experience -- combining the empirical description of social differences, inequalities, or lived mobility experiences among population groups with explicit ethical or normative reflection on the meaning, justice, dignity, care, responsibility, or human significance of mobility. This includes social exclusion, poverty, unequal accessibility, socio-spatial segregation, and differences in access to opportunities among groups defined by income, class, gender, age, disability, ethnicity, or other social positions, together with moral perception, virtue, care, hospitality, recognition, responsibility, alterity, and explicit reflection on justice, injustice, dignity, or the human meaning of movement and encounter.
dimensions.CONTACTO_EXPERIENCIAL: Empirical material generated by the researcher's own presence in the field, rather than obtained from records, sensors, registers, counts or administrative databases. Procedures include ethnographic fieldwork and prolonged immersion, participant and non-participant observation, field notes and field diaries, in-depth and semi-structured interviews with informants, focus groups and discussion groups, oral histories and biographical accounts, go-along, ride-along and walk-along methods in which the researcher accompanies the participant, diaries kept by the participants themselves, photo-elicitation and visual documentation produced during fieldwork, workshops and co-design sessions with local residents, participatory action research, purposive, theoretical and snowball sampling of informants, audio recording and verbatim transcription, open, axial and thematic coding of transcripts, grounded theory, discourse and narrative analysis, hermeneutic and phenomenological interpretation, theoretical saturation, triangulation of qualitative sources, reflexivity regarding the position of the researcher, and the presentation of findings through direct quotations from those interviewed.

_nivel2_referencia_no_usado_por_el_pipel._nota: Estos dos textos NO se usan: el loader solo lee 'relevance' y 'dimensions'. Se conservan como insumo para un eventual nivel 2 que separe lo social-descriptivo de lo etico-normativo dentro de SOCIAL_HUMANA.
_nivel2_referencia_no_usado_por_el_pipel.SOCIAL_DESCRIPTIVO: Urban mobility or transport examined as a socially differentiated phenomenon involving relations, practices, experiences, opportunities, or inequalities among population groups. The central concern is how mobility conditions and experiences vary according to income, social class, gender, age, disability, ethnicity, migration status, occupation, residential location, or other social positions. This includes social exclusion, poverty, transport disadvantage, unequal accessibility, socio-spatial segregation, everyday mobility practices, socially situated travel experiences and perceptions, and differences in access to destinations, services, employment, education, or other opportunities.
_nivel2_referencia_no_usado_por_el_pipel.ETICO_NORMATIVO: Urban mobility or transport examined through moral perception, affect, attentiveness, virtue, or character -- the lived, embodied, and relational encounter with other people, bodies, or places in urban space. This includes phenomenological or non-representational approaches to everyday mobility; sensitivity or attentiveness to the presence, situation, or vulnerability of another person while moving through the city; care, hospitality, recognition, responsiveness, and responsibility toward the other as the basis for judging whether a mobility practice is just, good, or right; and philosophical or ethical reflection on encounter, coexistence, dignity, autonomy, and the relation to the other -- where that relation itself, rather than a system to optimize or a population to describe, is the primary object of analysis.
